title: Linear Algebra via Exterior Products
note: Appendices (complex numbers, permutations, matrices, license) are not broken down. Summaries are in our own words; the text stays in the PDF.
summary: A coordinate-free course in linear algebra for physicists and mathematicians that does nearly everything with the exterior (wedge) product instead of matrices. After vector spaces, duals and tensor products, it introduces exterior powers and uses them to define determinants, the trace and the characteristic polynomial as basis-independent objects, then derives Cramer’s rule, Vandermonde determinants, Cayley–Hamilton, functions of operators, the Jacobi and Liouville formulas and the Jordan form. A final chapter adds a scalar product: orthogonality, Hodge-style duality, antisymmetric operators and Pfaffians.
